datums.A: Base bottom (primary). Print bed for the frame.
datums.B: Journal / cone axis (secondary). Common axis of the spinner.
datums.C: 3× Ø8 posts on Ø76 PCD at 120° (tertiary). Locates the top plate.

fits_mm.location_posts_plate: +0.40 diametral (Ø8.0 / Ø8.4), posts through the plate
fits_mm.location_bushing_seat: +0.40 diametral (Ø14.0 / Ø14.4) with a 2 mm land
fits_mm.centering_cone: 0.20 radial at the cup mouth (male r 4.8 in female r 5.0)
fits_mm.axial_thrust_and_cap: 0.20 float — running faces do not occupy the same volume

gdt.position: Post pattern positional Ø0.4 MMC to B (one nozzle). FDM cannot hold tighter without a gauge print.

lessons.title: Clearance is a design input
lessons.teach: A 0.4 mm Bambu nozzle cannot hold CNC fits. Model +0.40 mm diametral clearance in CAD for every printed-to-printed running or slip interface. Leave slicer XY hole compensation at 0 unless a gauge print says otherwise.

lessons.title: No FDM press fits
lessons.teach: Press fits fail from elephant foot and shrinkage. Use +0.40 slip and retain with a shoulder, land, plate, or cap. Do not assume a metal bearing will appear later.

lessons.title: Build a proper assembled stack
lessons.teach: Bodies sit on one axis with real location: posts go through the top plate (not a butt joint), the rotor sweep clears the posts, the bushing sits on a land (not a through-pocket), and running faces have modeled gaps. Assembly order: base → shaft → rotor → top plate → bushing → cap.

lessons.title: Print a thrust bearing that can actually spin
lessons.teach: A lifted same-angle cone never touches (parallel surfaces). Center with a 45° cup and a smaller male cone, and take thrust on a narrow annular land with 0.20 mm float. Relief under the apex so the tip does not bottom.

lessons.title: Keep the machine even
lessons.teach: Three posts at 120° and two rotor buckets at 180°. Double-D drive so the rotor turns the shaft. An odd one-sided vane will not run true.

lessons.title: Print the bearings too
lessons.teach: Printed cone + land for thrust, printed sleeve in a shouldered seat for radial. Plate thicker than the bushing so the seat has a land. Metal 608 / catalog bearings are a later table, not a hidden part.

lessons.title: The rotor is a part that mounts
lessons.teach: A lone C-loft coupon is not a rotor. The even spinner has a hub on a double-D, sitting on the shaft shoulder, with two helical buckets joined to that hub.

lessons.title: Export a printable package
lessons.teach: Assign appearances, run solid_export_preflight, then solid_export_3mf for bambu_studio. Print each body in its own orientation (base/plate flat, shaft on the land, bushing as a ring, rotor on the hub face). 3MF is the manufacturing handoff.
